newsitem.title: UK: Zurich takes long view on China.
newsitem.headline: Zurich takes long view on China.

text.p: Swiss insurer Zurich has set its sights on a licence to do business in China, but hopes for a broader remit than those issued to European and American insurers to date.
"I believe our strategy will be of long term benefit," chairman and chief executive Rolf Hueppi told a post results news conference in London on Wednesday.
Zurich has a larger, broader goal than other insurers which have mostly been given only limited licences to operate in the Shanghai region and with the foreign community, he added.
The company had a good relationship with the Chinese authorities, while its operations in Taiwan and Hong Kong gave it an excellent platform for eventual expansion in China, Hueppi said.

The company's China strategy reflects Hueppi's aim of doing more business with its existing customers by fostering long-term relationships and developing customer solutions rather than a range of standard products.
Hueppi said he saw many advantages flowing from dramatic changes in the financial services markets where the company operates.
In particular, he singled out asset management, reinsurance and new distribution methods in personal insurance.

In terms of geographic opportunities, Hueppi noted that developing markets in Asia, Latin America, Africa eastern and central Europe now accounted for 2.8 percent of business compared with 0.8 percent in 1991.
"I believe these areas will continue to grow rapidly, although their impact is not yet significant."
However, Zurich would continue to focus on return on investment rather than volume growth and had pulled out of some countries, while limiting itself to specific lines of business in many others.
"The emphasis is on narrow, defined markets. For example, we don't want to get into general insurance in Japan," where the company has a licence to do life insurance business, Hueppi said.
